# Verification ledger

Every acceptance check from `docs/PLAN.md` Part C lives here with its real status.
Statuses: **VERIFIED** (machine, date, evidence) · **CI** (verified by the named CI
job) · **NEEDS-DEVICE(os/hw)** (written and `cargo check`-ed, runtime not yet
exercised — the user or a Claude Code session on that machine clears it) · **OPEN**.

Dev machine for this ledger unless stated otherwise: the build VM — Ubuntu 26.04 LTS,
GNOME on Wayland, VMware virtual GPU (no hardware encoder), 4 vCPU / 7 GiB,
Rust stable 1.96. No sudo: FFmpeg / PipeWire / ALSA dev headers are unavailable
locally, so those backends are compiled and tested by the Linux CI job instead.

Host logged `answered ping #1`…`#5` both times. Final tree (run 8): connect 9.6 s, `PING OK n=3 min/avg/max=591.6/609.7/633.8 ms`, host `client disconnected after 3 ping(s)`, Ctrl-C ⇒ `Flushed persistent state at exit.`, exit 0, no stray output. Errors map to host-offline / host-not-running / timeout messages (`SignalError`); one real Tor transient (rendezvous circuit failure) was hit in 11 connects and reported as "Tor did not answer in time … retry". **Independently reproduced 2026-08-29** (fresh `target/tornect-test/v2` against the `v1` host above): cold bootstrap 8.7 s, connect **47.7 s**, `PING OK n=5 min/avg/max=844.6/947.3/1101.3 ms` (844.6 / 940.4 / 976.6 / 1101.3 / 873.5); against the restarted host, attempts 1 and 2 timed out at 60 s (`Tor did not answer in time…`, exit 1; host logged `hspool: Too many preemptive onion service circuits failed` and two HSDir upload timeouts) and attempt 3 connected in 5.7 s: `PING OK n=5 min/avg/max=539.5/560.7/617.1 ms` (550.1 / 539.5 / 549.9 / 617.1 / 546.7); host logged `answered ping #1`…`#5` and `client disconnected after 5 ping(s)` both times, exit 0. So on a bad Tor evening 2 of 4 connects fail and need the retry the message asks for; the "up to 2 min" / "≈ 70 s" reachability figures are typical, not bounds. | **A7** a newer signed `SESSION_REQUEST` pre-empts a stale charged handshake (§B.8.4.5, `PREEMPTED` 0x002A) | VERIFIED the build VM 2026-09-04 for the cancel; the newer request getting in VERIFIED (unit) 2026-10-24 (audit B03) | Found by the track C review: cancellation is the rule and `UA_BUSY` the narrow case, but only the narrow case was implemented, so `PREEMPTED` was emitted nowhere in the workspace and a client whose circuit died was locked out for the full 30 s `AwaitKe3` timeout. The budget table now carries a per-pk cancel handle and a `charged` flag and the exchange is raced against it. `unattended::tests::a_newer_request_preempts_a_stale_charged_handshake` — fails cleanly in ~2 s against a build with the cancel disabled (verified by mutation). **Corrected 2026-10-24 (audit B03):** the test checked only the stale stream's `PREEMPTED`, never the newer request, and the newer request was refused `NOT_GRANTED` 0x0010: it reached `limiter.charge` before the cancelled handshake had settled its charge, so the client was still turned away (and told its access was never given). Fixed in `ab16c6c9` (see B03 under *Audit fixes*): the test now also asserts that the newer request is accepted, with a multi-thread variant |

| PoW DoS defense + rate limits on | VERIFIED the build VM 2026-08-29 (configuration, admission policy, effort-ordered queue exercised live); OPEN: suggested-effort ramp under sustained load; OPEN: a cold Tornect client solving under a queue-filling flood (client-side follow-up, M1-4) | `tor-pow` feature default-on; service launched with `enable_pow=true`, `rate_limit_at_intro=(25/s, burst 200)`, `max_concurrent_streams_per_circuit=4`, `pow_rend_queue_depth=1024` (unit test `onion_service_config_builds_with_and_without_pow` reads every bound back from the built `OnionServiceConfig`); Arti wrote `hss/<nick>/pow_manager.json` + `pow_nonces/`. **Admission (third security review, high; decision M1-4)**: with PoW on the accept loop reserves a handshake *and* a circuit permit **before** polling Arti's request stream (`tor::Admission::Backpressure`, derived from the built config's `enable_pow`), so the overflow stays in Arti's effort-ordered, bounded (1024), expiring (300 s) queue — the only place Arti measures load and orders admission by proof-of-work; the second-review loop polled unconditionally and dropped the overflow itself, which kept that queue empty and the suggested effort at zero. With PoW off it drains and drops (`Admission::Drop`; Arti's PoW-off queue is an unbounded FIFO). Unit tests on the generic `supervise` loop with a poll-counting scripted stream: `backpressure_does_not_poll_the_request_stream_while_the_budget_is_full` (the stream is not polled while the one slot is held; the waiting request is served once it frees), `drop_policy_takes_every_request_and_drops_the_overflow`, `admission_follows_the_pow_setting_and_defaults_match_the_constants`. Live (`live_rendezvous_backpressure`, 2026-08-29 00:16 UTC, `target/tornect-test/review3-live2.log`): host published with a one-handshake / one-circuit budget (`TorNode::publish_with_limits`), three parallel `connect()`s from a second Tor node in the same process; the host accepted the three streams at 13.1 s, 21.3 s and 29.5 s (gaps 8.2 s and 8.3 s = 5 s hold + 2 s idle + handshake), every client got through on its first `connect()`, no request was dropped; one client's first introduction was refused by a stale intro point (`INTRODUCE_ACK: NOT_RECOGNIZED`) and Arti's retry carried a proof of work — `tor_hsclient::pow::v1: beginning solve, Effort(8) … solve complete … duration=11ms` — which the host verified and served: the effort-ordered path end to end — after a *fast* failure inside one Arti attempt series, the only path on which Tornect's client solves today (second OPEN item below). Host-side bounds after three security reviews (`tor::listener`, `ping`, unit-tested with scripted streams; decision M1-4): 32 rendezvous handshakes in flight (permit held only across `RendRequest::accept`, 30 s cap), 64 live rendezvous circuits, a circuit with no open signaling stream for 30 s is dropped (which closes it), a request that is not `BEGIN` on port 4000 destroys its circuit, a full accept queue refuses `BEGIN` with `END(DONE)` before accepting (10 s cap on `accept` and on `reject`), a stream write with no progress for 30 s fails with `TimedOut` on either side (`stall_timer_fails_a_write_with_no_progress_and_resets_on_progress`), and `ping::serve` disconnects a peer that sends nothing or takes no pong for 30 s (`stalled_pong_write_is_cut_after_the_deadline`), ends any session after 120 s or 100 pings (`chatty_client_is_cut_when_the_session_budget_is_spent`, `ping_budget_ends_the_session`) and reads at most 22-byte frames (`host_rejects_garbage`); `tornect host` serves at most 64 sessions at once. Residual exposure (M1-4): ≈ 1 dead-rendezvous-point introduction/s fills the handshake budget and ≈ 0.5 rendezvous/s the circuit budget — without PoW a lockout, with PoW an effort-ordered wait that a cold Tornect client cannot yet win (second OPEN item); per-device accounting is the envelope track's. **OPEN**: the suggested-effort *ramp* — Arti raises the published effort only for a 300 s period in which its queue was non-empty *and* at least `num_dequeued / busy_fraction` PoW-bearing requests arrived (`tor-hsservice-0.45.0/src/pow/v1.rs` 968–1036) — was not driven to a nonzero value here: the one-slot run lasted 35 s and `hss/<nick>/pow_manager.json` still holds `"suggested_effort": 0`. Recipe: `tornect host` with `TORNECT_LOG=info,tor_hsservice::pow=debug`; from another machine keep ≥ 40 `connect()` loops running against it for ≥ 10 min (more than the 32-handshake budget, so the host logs `rendezvous budget full; further requests wait in Tor's proof-of-work queue` — once per admitted request while saturated — and Arti's queue is non-empty for the update period; a Tor-side failure that surfaces *inside* one Arti connect attempt series makes the Arti client retry with effort ≥ 8 — a fast one such as `INTRODUCE_ACK: NOT_RECOGNIZED` does, a request that merely queues does not until Arti's rendezvous-completion timeout, ≈ 8 min on a cold estimator and so after `CONNECT_TIMEOUT`, and the effort resets on every `TorNode::connect()` (next OPEN item); only PoW-bearing arrivals count toward the ramp (`num_enqueued_gte_suggested`, 1150–1158), so run the loops from *warm* client state dirs — ≥ 100 recorded builds in `state/arti/state/circuit_timeouts.json`, so the rendezvous wait can end inside the 60 s and the retry solve — or the queue stays non-empty but PoW-free and the effort stays at 0); expect `suggested_effort` in `pow_manager.json` to become nonzero and new clients to log `beginning solve, Effort(N)` with N from the descriptor. A request whose client gave up while it queued still costs one circuit-build attempt when dequeued (`RendRequest` carries no receive time, `req.rs` 25–47), bounded by `RENDEZVOUS_TIMEOUT`. **OPEN (fourth security review, medium; decision M1-4)**: honest-client effort under a queue-filling flood. The third-review text said a client whose request went unanswered retries with effort ≥ 8; verified from the sources, that retry lives inside one Arti connect attempt series only (`HsPowClient` per series at the descriptor's suggested effort, `tor-hsclient-0.45.0/src/connect.rs` 929; no PoW state in the per-service `Data`, 78–125; a fresh isolation group per `TorNode::connect()`, `node.rs` 311, starts from a blank record, `state.rs` 561), and an *unanswered* request fails only by `RendezvousCompletionTimeout` after `rpt_ipt_timeout` = 3 × `BuildCircuit { length: 5 }` + 1 × `OneWay` estimates (`connect.rs` 1481–1518), which the Pareto estimator answers with the 60 s `cbtinitialtimeout` fallback scaled by length (≈ 3 × 150 s + 40 s ≈ 8 min) until it has `cbtmincircs` = 100 recorded builds (`tor-circmgr-0.45.0/src/timeouts/pareto.rs` 524–533, 617–638; the nine logged `tornect ping` runs left 55 in `target/tornect-test/h2/state/arti/state/circuit_timeouts.json`). `CONNECT_TIMEOUT` = 60 s bounds the whole connect (`node.rs` 314–336) and the CLI does not retry a `Timeout` (`tor_cmd.rs` 188, 297): a cold client's effort-0 request is the youngest of its class in Arti's queue, displaced by the next arrival once the 1024-deep queue is full (`pow/v1.rs` 1169–1177), and the client starts again at effort 0 on the next call. The low-rate flood of the third review *is* fixed (FIFO wait in Arti's queue, nothing dropped); the effort-ordered queue is not yet reachable by a cold Tornect client on the slow path. Not a listener change: the client-side follow-up (retries under a longer deadline inside `TorNode::connect` when the descriptor carries `pow-params`, or a Tornect-level effort floor across calls, which needs Arti to persist or accept a client effort) is tracked in M1-4 for the envelope track. Recipe (extends the one above): while the host logs `rendezvous budget full`, start one **cold** client — a fresh `TORNECT_HOME` (e.g. `target/tornect-test/cold`, no `state/arti/state/circuit_timeouts.json`) — with `TORNECT_LOG=info,tor_hsclient::pow=debug tornect ping <id>`; expect `tor_hsclient::pow::v1: beginning solve, Effort(N)` (N ≥ 8, or the descriptor's effort once the ramp is nonzero) within `CONNECT_TIMEOUT` (60 s) and a `connected in … s` line. As of this ledger it fails instead with `Tor did not answer in time` after 60 s without ever logging `beginning solve`; the item closes when that step passes |

Recipe: on a Windows 10 20H1+ machine, the cross-built `tornect.exe host` (or `cargo run -p tornect -- host` there) with no `TORNECT_HOME`; expect `Tornect ID:` then `REACHABLE` within ~2 min; from a second machine `tornect ping <id> --count 3` → `PING OK`; kill and restart the host → same ID; `icacls %LOCALAPPDATA%\Tornect\arti` must list only the user, `SYSTEM` and `Administrators` (if it lists `Users`/`Everyone`, add an explicit owner-only DACL in `create_private_dir` — `windows-sys` `SetNamedSecurityInfoW` — and record it in docs/DEPENDENCIES.md); if the host logs a HashX/`dynasmrt` JIT failure (PoW compiles a hash function into executable memory), `hashx` falls back to its interpreter by itself (`hashx-0.9.1/src/lib.rs` 76 `TryCompiler`), and `disable_pow_compilation = true` in `onion_service_config` is the explicit fallback — record which happened |

The HashX JIT (`dynasmrt` → `memmap2` RWX mapping) is the platform risk: a hardened-runtime build without the `com.apple.security.cs.allow-jit` entitlement fails the mapping, which `hashx` handles by falling back to the interpreter (`hashx-0.9.1/src/lib.rs` 76) — slower puzzle verification, not a crash — and `disable_pow_compilation = true` is the explicit fallback (docs/research/arti.md §16.8). Recipe: on macOS 13+ (Apple silicon), `cargo run -p tornect -- host`; expect `Tornect ID:` then `REACHABLE` within ~2 min; from a second machine `tornect ping <id> --count 3` → `PING OK`; kill/restart → same ID; `ls -ld ~/Library/Application\ Support/Tornect/state/arti` → `drwx------`; run once more with `RUST_LOG=hashx=debug` while a client connects and record whether the compiler or the interpreter was used; for the notarized M8 build, decide entitlement vs `disable_pow_compilation` from that |
| `cargo deny check` (advisories, bans, licenses, sources) | VERIFIED the build VM 2026-08-28 | cargo-deny 0.20.2 (prebuilt musl binary under `target/tools/`, not installable via apt here): `advisories ok, bans ok, licenses ok, sources ok`; the two advisory ignores in `deny.toml` (RUSTSEC-2023-0071 `rsa` via Arti's ssh-key fork, RUSTSEC-2024-0436 `paste`) are the only ones needed; 36 `duplicate` warnings (`multiple-versions = "warn"`: RustCrypto 0.10/0.11 and rand 0.8/0.10 lines coexisting under Arti, docs/research/arti.md §3) and 6 unused license allowances; `bans.allow-wildcard-paths = true` added because the workspace's own version-less `path` dependencies were reported as wildcards. Output: `target/tornect-test/cargo-deny.log` |
| No OpenSSL / aws-lc in the dependency graph (`docs/research/arti.md` §2, `quic.md` §2) | VERIFIED the build VM 2026-08-28 | `cargo tree -i aws-lc-sys -p tornect-signal` and `cargo tree -i openssl-sys --workspace` both report `did not match any packages`; provider is `ring 0.17.14` via `rustls 0.23.43`. Now a gate: `cargo xtask verify` runs `cargo tree --workspace -i {aws-lc-rs, aws-lc-sys, openssl-sys}` and fails if any resolves; `install_crypto_provider` logs an already-installed foreign provider at `warn` with its name, and the unit test `install_is_idempotent_and_ring_is_the_provider_in_force` asserts the provider in force is `Ring` |

### The sharing indicator window (§B.6, UI_PLAN §6.3; 2026-09-23)

While any session runs, attended or unattended, control or view-only, a second small window titled
"Tornect: sharing" shows who, which mode and the clock, with **Stop**. It is always-on-top, has no
decorations, has a fixed size, sits at the top-right of the primary monitor and is not activated when
it opens (on X11 it is a utility window); the main window keeps its banner (`apps/tornect/src/ui/indicator.rs`). Its Stop is the
banner's Stop: the host-wide kill with `BYE{USER}`. Closing the window does nothing while the screen
is shared. A press-and-drag anywhere but Stop moves it.

| Check | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|

A mode change is capture reporting input injected or not injected, or a view-only session taking a control session's place; the clock ticking alone is no change. The model keeps every shared session in a list (`Model::sharing`), so a session never drops off the indicator while another overlaps it |

`bin` on `PATH`, `TMPDIR=$PWD/target/tmp`, 2 jobs, each build in its own `systemd-run --user --scope`

`818bb8a`, `787b5da`. Full evidence: `/home/mx/kore_project_V3/agents/classical_coder/reports/2026-09-23_windows_build.md`.

Now a tokio task waits for the signal (`ui::quit_requested`) and wakes the event loop with `Wake::Quit`, which takes the close button's path (`App::quit`: every session ended with a goodbye, at most 10 s). On that path the hosted sessions end first, then the viewed session's goodbye gets up to 6 s (review N-4: in the other order a remote controller kept this desktop for those seconds when Tor stalled the goodbye): `ui::backend::tests::closing_ends_the_hosted_session_before_the_viewed_goodbye` (failing first: with the old order the host-wide kill had not fired 200 ms into a stalled goodbye). A kill ends only the sessions armed before it, so the shutdown fires it again every 100 ms while the goodbye waits, once more after it, and on every pass of the 3 s grace (the CLI host's grace too): a session that goes live after the first kill (a peer with unattended rights, a consent clicked while the window closes) ends within 100 ms (review P2-I4): `a_session_that_goes_live_during_the_goodbye_is_ended_too` (failing first: a guard armed 200 ms into a stalled goodbye was not killed within 1 s). `ui::tests::a_terminate_signal_is_a_quit_request` sends the test process a real SIGTERM and sees the request (the process survives it). `host::tests::what_a_killed_host_leaves_behind_never_blocks_the_next`: with a stale `host.lock` (a dead pid) and a stale `ipc.sock` (a socket nobody listens on) in place, `HostLock::acquire` and the control channel both come up: the lock is an OS lock that dies with its process, and a socket that refuses connections is replaced; the CLI host's clean exit also leaves both files (live run in the service row), with the same result. Not handled: the Windows console's close button, logoff and shutdown events (E2-6, disclosed). Recipe: start `tornect` (the window) hosting, open a session from a second device, then `kill -TERM <pid>` (and, in another run, Ctrl-C in the terminal that started it): the viewer gets the session's end, the window closes within 10 s, and `sessions.log` has the session's end record; start the window again at once: it hosts. Live on the build VM 2026-09-24 (the console check's fourth attempt, `37a70e1`): the windows started at 16:04:20 in homes where the `6b0da44` windows' SIGTERM at 01:21 had left `host.lock`, `unattended.lock` and `ipc.sock`; both hosts logged `IPC endpoint listening`, took the lock (the new pid in `host.lock`) and published their old IDs. SIGTERM at 16:44:21 to the Wayland host and the client (no session live): both logged `asked to quit by a signal: ending every session`, stopped the onion service and Tor and ended within 0.3 s; the three files stay on disk after that exit too. Not run live: SIGINT, and a signal during a live session |

`apps/tornect/src/history.rs` `Pins`) and the host handshake's `TrustedDeviceStore::touch` (`DevicePins`; since

## History off by default (the operator's ruling of 2026-09-28)

"Off by default (Recommended)" — "Nothing about past connections is written unless you switch history on in Settings;
the first run says so in one line." The switch is the address book's `history` (M-UI-2); the first-run line on Home is
M-UI-3's. Superseded in its wording on 2026-09-29 (F4-M1): the switch covers the recent list only, and the session log
records requests to this computer, and this computer's unattended connections to others, whatever it says.

## The Windows administrator helper (M-FEAT-3; 2026-09-29)

`tornect input-helper`, the only elevated part of Tornect, and everything around it (`docs/PLAN.md` §B.2.1,
§B.8.7.5, §B.8.8, §B.8.13; decisions M1-57, M1-62): the frame protocol and the helper's loop
(`crates/tornect-input/src/helper.rs`), the pipe, the launch and the checks (`crates/tornect-platform/src/helper.rs`,
`win_helper.rs`), the on-demand task (`helper_task.rs`, `win_task.rs`), the FSM seam between the answer and the
accept (`crates/tornect-signal/src/fsm/host.rs`), the host's side (`apps/tornect/src/admin_helper.rs`), the command
(`helper_cmd.rs`), the secure-screen watch (`secure_screen.rs`), and the carried items of step 0. **Every Windows call is
type-checked only on the build VM** (no Windows machine); every decision is a pure function tested here, the channel
end to end over a Unix socket pair standing in for the named pipe.

**`ADMIN_HELPER` stays `false` in this build:** switching it on makes the installed row offer "Allow as administrator…"
and the no-prompt row its answer, and two existing sheet tests of M-FEAT-2 pin the build without the helper
(`view::tests::the_session_sheet_offers_only_the_levels_of_its_row`: `!prompt.has("Allow as administrator…")`;
`consent::tests::a_session_sheet_carries_its_levels_and_drops_them`: `SheetLevels::of(&prompt).answers.admin == None`).
The brief keeps trust-surface tests unchanged and says to stop and report instead; with the flag set on the tree of
`19cb0de`, every other test passes (`cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast`: 810 passed, 2 failed — those two —
6 ignored; `target/tmp/feat3-flip-tests-kept.log`). Until the flag is on, the sheet hides the answer and says why, and
the helper path of the FSM is unreachable.

**The Windows recipe (NEEDS-DEVICE(windows), the operator's PC, after the flag is on):** install to `C:\Program Files\Tornect`;
(1) an administrator account, UAC at its default: a second device asks for a session, "Allow as administrator…",
Windows' consent prompt on the secure desktop; Yes: the session starts, the banner says "as administrator", the
viewer's clicks reach an elevated `regedit` or an elevated `cmd`; `sessions.log` has `admin_helper_started` and
`session_started` with `"elevation":"admin"`; Task Manager shows one `tornect.exe` running elevated for the session only;
(2) the same, No at Windows' prompt: the sheet comes back with "Administrator access was not given", the other answers,
armed after a second; the popup's time keeps running; (3) a standard account: Windows asks for an administrator's name
and password; the session's input reaches elevated windows; (4) panic key, the window's Stop and `tornect panic` with an
elevated window focused: the session ends and the elevated `tornect.exe` is gone within 2 s; (5) kill the host from
Task Manager during an administrator session: the helper exits (pipe closed or host exit); (6) with a secure screen
(Ctrl+Alt+Del, a UAC prompt) during a Control session: the window's events say the notice; (7) `PromptOnSecureDesktop` 0:
the sheet says Windows' prompts appear on the shared screen, and whether the viewer can answer a prompt drawn there
(if yes, those machines join the UAC-off row); (8) an older version's elevated start-at-login task, then
`tornect service install`: Windows' prompt removes it, `schtasks /Query /TN Tornect /XML` shows `LeastPrivilege`;
(9) Windows 11's administrator protection, if the PC has it: whether the helper's checks still pass;
(10) once admin grants exist (M-FEAT-5): the task appears with the first admin grant, disappears with the last, is
disabled while unattended access is off, and an unattended administrator session starts through it, or at none with
"administrator access unavailable" when it does not connect within 5 s.

The gate is green at **814 passed, 0 failed, 6 ignored** at `4699f2a` (2026-09-29), each commit of M-FEAT-3
gate-green on its own tree before it was committed. Two hardening commits after the screenshots: the helper pipe's
writes wait at most 2 s (`af3c668`), and the helper's threads have explicit stack sizes, so the standard library reads
no `RUST_MIN_STACK` in the elevated process (`4d5878e`).

## Before the tag: the carried findings of M-UI-3 and M-FEAT-3 (2026-09-29)

One question at a time on the request sheet, and the carried findings of M-UI-3 (U3-M1, U3-L2, U3-L3, F-3 of its
trust surfaces, the scam window) and M-FEAT-3 (F-1, F-2, F-3, F-4, F-8), each in its own commit, each gate-green on its

## Unattended host completeness (M-FEAT-5; 2026-10-02)

Decision M1-67 (`docs/PLAN.md` row 7), each commit gate-green on its own tree. `ADMIN_HELPER` stays false; no manifest
change. **The client's rule** (`crates/tornect-core/src/unattended/{credentials,hosts}.rs`,
`crates/tornect-signal/src/fsm/{mod,client,tests}.rs`, `apps/tornect/src/{ua_client,tor_cmd,host}.rs`,
`apps/tornect/src/ui/backend.rs`): the client decides about a remembered password from the host's verified answer
alone, before QUIC. Until the wire carries `grant_reach`, every unattended answer reads as one that leaves the key
out: nothing is kept, and a remembered password is deleted at the answer. Existing tests changed, each named in its
row: two rewritten for the new rule (`unattended::credentials::tests::{remember_is_offered_only_with_a_keychain_and_never_for_administrator_without_a_gate, an_administrator_grant_keeps_no_password_without_a_presence_gate}`),

(`Attempt::Accepted { elevation, grant_reach }`, `settle`'s new argument and result) in
`unattended::credentials::tests::{a_password_is_kept_after_an_accept_and_stale_only_when_refused, forget_deletes_the_entry_and_the_flag}`,
`ua_client::tests::{a_failed_save_leaves_no_password_behind, forget_deletes_the_password_when_the_file_cannot_be_read, rotate_id_deletes_every_hosts_password_whatever_its_flag, a_remembered_password_that_vanished_is_asked_for_again, only_a_refusal_of_the_remembered_password_deletes_it, unreachable_wrong_password_and_a_broken_stream_read_differently}`

## Before the tag: the control channel, the block window, the panic key and four corrections

The operator's rulings of 2026-10-03 and 2026-10-05 (decision M1-69; `docs/PLAN.md` §B.8.6.3, §B.8.7.4, §B.8.9.1 and
Part C row 9a), each commit gate-green on its own tree. `ADMIN_HELPER` stays false; the administrator helper's pipe and
the Unix socket are unchanged. The Windows calls are type-checked (`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --target
x86_64-pc-windows-gnullvm`); no test makes one.

| Check | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| The Windows control pipe gets a fresh random name at each host start (§B.8.7.4): `\\.\pipe\tornect-ctl-` and the 32 lowercase hex digits of 16 random bytes, never the administrator helper's prefix; once the first instance exists the host writes the name into `<state_dir>\ipc.pipe` with the pipe's this-account-only descriptor (a new temporary file, written, flushed, then moved over the name file), and without that file it has no channel; the endpoint removes the file when dropped if it still holds its name; the command line takes the name from that file only: no file is no host, and anything but exactly such a name is refused before a pipe is opened; no code computes a name from the state directory any more | VERIFIED (unit) for the name, the file's write, read and removal; the calls type-checked; NEEDS-DEVICE(windows) | `ipc::pipe_rules::{a_control_pipe_name_is_random_each_time, the_name_file_round_trips, no_name_file_means_no_host, a_name_file_that_is_not_a_control_pipe_is_refused}` (platform; every system; failed first on 2026-10-05). Device: start `tornect host`, stop it, start it again: `[System.IO.Directory]::GetFiles("\\.\pipe\")` shows a `tornect-ctl-` name that differs at each start; `icacls %LOCALAPPDATA%\Tornect\ipc.pipe` shows this account only; from a second account the file cannot be read; `tornect panic` and `tornect unattended status` answer; once the host has stopped, the file is gone |
| A name file left by a host that did not stop cleanly is trusted only for a pipe of this account (§B.8.7.4): the command line counts the pipe the name file names as a running host only once it opened it and the account of its server, read from the server's process id, is this account, the check a request makes before anything is sent; a pipe that another account made since under that name, or one whose server's account or process cannot be read, is no host, so the command line falls to the host lock, and to the offline guard when no host holds it; a pipe whose every instance is busy still counts as a host | VERIFIED (unit) for the decision; the calls type-checked; NEEDS-DEVICE(windows) | `ipc::pipe_rules::a_pipe_of_another_account_is_no_running_host` (platform; every system). Device: `taskkill /F` the host, create its dead `tornect-ctl-` pipe from a second account, run `tornect unattended off`: it must fall to the offline guard |
| A request whose block window could not be shown is refused (§B.8.6.3): the window host's block window counts as shown only once one of its windows drew its first frame (reported where the app paints the block windows; a window created but never drawn counts for nothing) or, on Linux, once the notification server showed its notification; with neither before the window's end, or as soon as every window failed to open and no notification is up or coming, the request is refused `HOST_NOT_READY` without a `cause` before any accept, one `HostNotReady` line names the device, and the grant is left as it was (nothing is suspended, unlike a Block); a Block at the same moment still blocks; the terminal host's rule is unchanged (a block line it cannot write, or a closed terminal, refuses as a Block) | VERIFIED (unit); NEEDS-DEVICE(windows), NEEDS-DEVICE(gnome) | `ui::block::tests::a_block_window_shown_nowhere_refuses_the_request`, `ui::app::tests::a_block_surface_that_fails_reports_it` (apps/tornect), `fsm::tests::a_block_window_not_shown_is_refused_and_the_grant_stays` (tornect-signal; all failed first on 2026-10-05); for "a window created but never drawn counts for nothing", `ui::app::tests::a_block_window_that_opened_is_not_shown_until_it_draws` (apps/tornect; the windows that opened are kept through the same code as the app's GPU windows, which reports nothing for them; failed first on 2026-10-07 with a report of a drawn frame added where an opened window is kept). Device, on Windows and on Linux: with an unattended grant whose block window is 5 s, make the block window fail to open (on Linux a session whose compositor refuses new windows, with no notification daemon running; on Windows a window host whose GPU surface cannot be created) and connect from the other device: the client is refused as not ready, `tornect unattended status` shows the grant still active, and `tornect unattended log` has a `host_not_ready` line for that device; with the windows working, the same connect shows the block window and starts after 5 s |
| Every operation on `hosts.toml` (the remembered passwords' records and the pin of each host's key) holds, beside this process's mutex, an OS lock on `hosts.toml.lock` next to it (§B.8.9.1): created this account's only if missing, taken exclusively, tried every 50 ms for at most 10 s, released when the operation ends; so the window and a command line never save over each other. A lock not taken in time fails the operation with "another Tornect held the lock beside hosts.toml for more than 10 s; nothing was saved", and one that cannot be opened or taken at all with "the lock beside hosts.toml could not be taken (<why>); nothing was saved": nothing saves without it. The pin check then answers as for an unreadable file, a mismatch (no proof is sent, never "no pin yet", which would trust a new host key), and the pin's record writes nothing; Forget, Rotate ID and the settling of an answer still delete a remembered password first, as they do when `hosts.toml` cannot be read. ## The viewer toolbar (M-UI-4 of the redesign; 2026-10-08)

The stream window's slim bar becomes the redesign's floating toolbar (decision M1-70; `docs/PLAN.md` Part C row 8,
§B.2.1, §B.8.8), in `apps/tornect/src/ui/{pages/viewer,stream,keys,app,view,model}.rs`, and then gains the
screenshot (`ui/screenshot.rs`), the host's notice code (`PONG` key 1, §B.8.4.1: `crates/tornect-signal`,
`apps/tornect/src/secure_screen.rs`, both hosts, `ui/backend.rs`), the lines it carries, Ctrl+Alt+Del by the host's
platform and full screen, with two carried corrections; each commit gate-green on its own tree. The Windows code is
type-checked (`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnullvm`); no test
makes a Windows call, and no test opens a window, an event loop or an injection: the egui pass runs headless with its
accessibility tree, and the forwarder and the chord are pure.

## Settings, sessions and the grant wizard (M-UI-5 of the redesign; 2026-10-08)

The Settings page replaces its placeholder (`docs/PLAN.md` Part C row 10, as the operator ruled on 2026-10-07; decision
M1-71) with the sections that need no operation of §B.8.6.2: General, Connection, Display and quality, Privacy and
About, in `apps/tornect/src/ui/pages/settings/`, a settings change saved by the tokio side (`ui/backend.rs`), the
redacted diagnostics report (`apps/tornect/src/diagnostics.rs`), the viewer opening from its saved defaults
(`ui/pages/viewer.rs`) and the first run's question (`ui/pages/home.rs`, `ui/backend.rs`); each commit gate-green on
its own tree. The Windows code is type-checked only; no test opens a window, starts Tor or writes outside a temporary
home.

| B01 Windows GDI capture took the secure desktop (a UAC prompt, Ctrl+Alt+Del, the lock screen) for a fatal error, so the whole session ended | VERIFIED (unit) 2026-10-22 for the wait-out; NEEDS-DEVICE(windows) on a real host; the end at a lock OPEN 2026-10-24 (the next row) | `56c3ef79`. A failed grab waits the caller's timeout and answers no new picture; a picture ends the spell; only a minute of failures in a row ends capture, with the grab's error. Tests: `outage::tests::{a_failed_grab_waits_and_says_no_new_picture, only_a_spell_that_lasts_the_limit_ends_capture, the_default_limit_is_a_minute}` (tornect-capture, the logic factored out of `gdi.rs`), `tests::a_source_with_no_picture_for_a_while_keeps_the_session` (tornect-session); `cargo clippy --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnullvm -p tornect-capture -p tornect-session --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean. Recipe: on Windows 10 20H1+ and 11, `tornect.exe host`, a Control session from Linux. (1) From the viewer start an elevated program (`powershell Start-Process cmd -Verb RunAs`): the session stays up, the picture stands still, within about 10 s the viewer says "The computer is showing a secure Windows screen; the person there must answer it"; answer Yes at the host within a minute: the picture moves again and the viewer toasts "The secure Windows screen closed"; the host's log has one "the screen cannot be read" warning and one "the screen can be read again" line. (2) The same with Ctrl+Alt+Del at the host, then Cancel. (3) Leave a prompt up past 60 s: the session ends "screen capture failed" about a minute after it appeared. (4) Win+L: the session ends about a minute later (`BYE{HOST_LOCKED}` is still the plan's, §B.8.8); unlocked within the minute, the picture comes back. (5) Throughout, the host process does not hold a core (Task Manager). Note whether `BitBlt` fails during the prompt or copies a black picture (either keeps the session) |
| B01 review: a Windows host that locks ends its sessions about a minute late, not at once with `BYE{HOST_LOCKED}` (§B.8.6.4; the §B.8.8 row "Windows, locked") | OPEN 2026-10-24 | Before `56c3ef79` the lock screen ended a session at once, by accident (`CAPTURE_FAILED` at the first failed grab). The wait-out cannot tell the lock screen from a UAC prompt or the Ctrl+Alt+Del screen (all three are the Winlogon desktop to `OpenInputDesktop`), so a locked host keeps a session, an unattended one included, with its picture standing still for up to `OUTAGE_LIMIT` (60 s); unlocked within that minute, the session goes on, input included (none reaches the secure desktop meanwhile: UIPI). A GDI failure with no secure desktop also stands still for that minute before capture ends. No interface promises that a lock ends a session; the B01 recipe's step (4) says what happens today. To do: the plan's lock watch (`WTSRegisterSessionNotification`'s `WTS_SESSION_LOCK`, or the `SessionFlags` of `WTSQuerySessionInformationW(WTSSessionInfoEx)`) ends every session `BYE{HOST_LOCKED}` at once, the wait-out kept for UAC and Ctrl+Alt+Del; whether an attended session ends at the lock too is to be decided with it (the plan's sentence is the unattended one). Recipe (Windows 10 20H1+ and 11): `tornect.exe host`, an unattended session from Linux, Win+L at the host: today the session ends about a minute later, "screen capture failed"; with the watch, at once, the viewer told the host locked |

| B02 A Tor bootstrap, publish or listener failure was terminal: the window stayed offline until Tornect was restarted | VERIFIED (unit) 2026-10-24 for the retry timer (`Restarting<T>`), the countdown, the model and the pages; the run loop's wiring by review only; review fixes VERIFIED (unit) 2026-10-24; a real outage NEEDS-DEVICE(linux-desktop) | `afa549c5`. After a failure (an error or a panic) the next try waits 30 s, doubling to at most 5 min, reset by a start that works (`Restarting<T>`; since `2011f4c9`, one that stayed up 5 min, below); Tor's start and the publishing of this ID each have one, and a listener that closes counts as a failed publish; each Tor try builds its ladder from the start's configuration, so decision M1-40 holds for every try. Home and Settings, Connection say what to check in plain words (no command, file or setting key), count down to the next try and offer "Try again now" (`Command::RetryTor`, which does nothing while a start runs). Tests: `ui::backend::tests::{the_retry_wait_doubles_up_to_five_minutes, a_failed_start_is_tried_again_after_its_wait, try_again_ends_the_wait_and_only_the_wait, the_model_through_a_failure_and_its_try, a_tor_failure_is_said_in_plain_words}`, `ui::pages::tests::a_tor_failure_counts_down_to_its_next_try_and_offers_one_now`. Corrected 2026-10-24 (review): no test drives `run`'s select loop (a due try calling `spawn_tor` again, a closed listener arming the publish, Try again now reaching Tor or the publish): the loop holds a real `TorNode` and `OnionListener`, which no test builds without Tor, so that wiring is checked by review, and by the recipe below. Review fixes `2011f4c9`: (1) a publish that returned reset the count, so an onion service that stops at once after each publish was published again every 30 s for good; a start's failure is the first in a row again only once it stayed up `STAYED_UP` (5 min), so such a service backs off to 5 min; (2) Settings, Connection drew "Try again now" for a publish's try under "Tor: connected"; it shows it for Tor's try only (Home keeps it beside the hosting line). Tests: `ui::backend::tests::{a_publish_that_stops_at_once_keeps_backing_off, a_failed_start_is_tried_again_after_its_wait}`, `ui::pages::tests::a_tor_failure_counts_down_to_its_next_try_and_offers_one_now` (extended). Not covered: the headless `tornect host` still exits when Tor does not start, and the older `tornect-host.service` unit restarts it only after a crash (`Restart=on-abnormal`; `afa549c5`'s message says systemd's `Restart=` applies, which is wrong for this unit, as `2011f4c9`'s says); the sign-in start (XDG autostart on Linux, the at-logon task on Windows) runs the window, `--background`. Recipe: on a GNOME desktop with the network off (`nmcli networking off`), start `tornect --background` hosting: once every way into Tor has failed (at most about 6 minutes) Home says "Tor: not reachable. Check that this computer is online. … Trying again in 30 s." with "Try again now", and incoming requests are off; turn the network on (`nmcli networking on`): at the next try (at most 5 min later), or at once with Try again now, Tor is ready, the hosting line goes to publishing and then reachable, and `tornect ping <id>` from another device answers, without restarting Tornect |

| B03 Unattended pre-emption answered the reconnecting request `NOT_GRANTED` instead of letting it in, and the A7 test never checked the new request | VERIFIED (unit) 2026-10-24; review fix VERIFIED (unit) 2026-10-24 | `ab16c6c9`. The pre-empting stream waits, at most 5 s (`PREEMPT_SETTLE`), for the cancelled handshake to settle its charge before it charges its own, and past the bound is answered the retryable `UA_BUSY`; a charge refusal that is not the gate's (a charge still pending, a store write that failed) is `UA_BUSY`, never `NOT_GRANTED`; the cancel is level-triggered (a flag plus `Notify`, the waiter enabled before the flag is read), so a pre-emption between `mark_charged` and the first poll of the `AwaitKe3` race on another worker thread is not lost; a handler dropped while charged and unsettled settles its charge as `disconnected` (it used to stay pending and refuse the device until the next restart). Tests (tornect-signal): `unattended::tests::{a_newer_request_preempts_a_stale_charged_handshake, a_preemption_across_worker_threads_lets_the_newer_request_in, a_preemption_before_the_stale_handshake_waits_still_cancels_it, a_charge_still_pending_is_answered_busy_never_not_granted, a_handshake_dropped_while_charged_settles_its_charge}`, each seen failing against a mutant of its fix (the wait removed, the waiter not enabled, the busy answer turned back into `NOT_GRANTED`, the drop's settle removed). The A7 row above is corrected. Not decided here (a policy question, left as the plan has it): whether a ladder lock armed by the stale charge should stop the pre-empting request at the gate. Review fix `5d7f0b1c`: the wait put up to 5 s between the gate and the charge, and a `debug_assert` that the gate's grant is the charged one panicked the handler (debug builds, tests) when the owner revoked and granted the device again meanwhile; the gate's grant is no longer kept, and what must hold, that the PAKE runs on the charged grant's record (read outside the limiter's lock just before the charge), is checked at run time: on a mismatch the charge is settled and the request answered `UA_BUSY`. Test: `unattended::tests::a_grant_renewed_while_a_preemption_settles_is_the_one_used` (panicked on the assertion) |

Corrected 2026-10-24 (review): what is not covered. The cooldown follows a session whose length, so counted from the PAKE success (`last_used.at`), reached `max_session_secs`, however it ended; no host cuts a session at its signed `ends_at` yet (the open M-FEAT-3 F-4 item). A session whose host process ends abruptly (killed, crashed, the machine switched off) records no end, so no cooldown follows it, even after a full-length session. A wall clock that jumps forward during a session counts it longer, which may give a cooldown to a shorter one |

Review fixes, 2026-10-24: (1) `f3c220ed`: this device's own `UnattendedConnect` lines (`tornect connect --unattended`, the window's unattended connects and admin commands) were written untagged through a handle without `K_log`, which the verifier, once wired, read as "untagged line after the chain started" at every start of a host with unattended access on; the window now writes them through its host role's store (tagged, the head kept, one writer in the process) and a process without a host keys its own handle with the home's `K_log` (`GrantStore::current_log_key`; untagged only where the host writes untagged lines, nothing written while `K_master` exists but cannot be read). Tests: `host::tests::this_devices_connect_lines_keep_the_log_intact` (fails with the old writer), `ua_client::tests::a_line_without_a_host_is_keyed_as_the_store_keys_its_own`, `ui::backend::tests::the_window_logs_its_connects_through_its_host_role` (tornect). (3) `98fe8658`: the load itself can append lines before the start's verifier runs (an abandoned charge settled, a machine-id change, a clock anomaly, lines held while the keystore was locked), each linking to the file's tail, so a tail cut while no host ran read as a whole chain; a host load now verifies the log before its first append and the start reports a break found there (`GrantStore::take_found_log`). Tests: `unattended::tests::b13_the_host_load_judges_the_log_before_its_own_lines` (tornect-core), `host::tests::a_cut_tail_is_reported_although_the_load_appends_first` (tornect; read Ok before). Not changed: two processes appending to one home's log at the same moment (a window host and a terminal's `tornect connect`) can still fork the chain, since no lock spans processes; a live log whose tail is cut while the host runs is healed by the next append (the verifier then finds a whole chain) |

| B08 The Windows panic-key hook kept Ctrl and Alt held after Ctrl+Alt+Del, so a later Ctrl+End, or a bare End, pressed the panic key (pressed twice: unattended access off, persisted) | VERIFIED (unit) 2026-10-24 for the modifier logic; both hooks NEEDS-DEVICE(windows) | `1bf717d7`, `981a7f4d`. A low-level hook is not called while the secure desktop takes the input, so the key-ups of Ctrl+Alt+Del (and of keys let go during a UAC prompt or on the lock screen) never reached it. As the chord's key goes down, the host's hook and the administrator helper's chord hook now read the system's key state (`GetAsyncKeyState`): a modifier the hook saw go down counts only while the system still has it down, and one it has up is forgotten. Injected events still never make a modifier count; a modifier with an injected event since its last physical one keeps what the hook saw until its next physical event, so a remote viewer's injected key-ups cannot hold the panic key off. That rule also keeps a stale modifier counted while the viewer's injected events of it keep the system's state out of the question: after Ctrl+Alt+Del, a Control-session viewer's Ctrl+C and Alt+Tab made the owner's bare End the chord again (Ctrl+End needed only Alt injected), found in review. So each hook's thread also sets an out-of-context WinEvent hook for `EVENT_SYSTEM_DESKTOPSWITCH`, and every switch of the input desktop forgets all the hook saw (`Modifiers::desktop_switched`); a chord pressed afresh after the switch works at once. The logic is `hotkey::Modifiers`, shared by both hooks (one thread-local, `hotkey::win::MODS`). Not covered: a modifier whose key-up the hook misses without a desktop switch (for example, should the host's medium-integrity hook miss keys while an elevated window has focus, UNVERIFIED in §B.8.7.5) still stays counted after the viewer injects that modifier, until its next physical event; and should `EVENT_SYSTEM_DESKTOPSWITCH` not reach the hook across the secure desktop, the Ctrl+Alt+Del case above is open again (recipe step 7 tells). Tests (tornect-platform): `hotkey::tests::{a_modifier_let_go_on_the_secure_desktop_does_not_linger, injected_modifiers_neither_press_nor_hold_off_the_panic_key, a_desktop_switch_forgets_modifiers_injected_input_kept_stale, the_chord_names_its_modifier_bits}` (the first two fail when the system's state is ignored, the third when a desktop switch forgets nothing); `cargo clippy --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnullvm -p tornect-platform --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean. Recipe (adds to TM-61): on Windows 10 20H1+ and 11, a host with unattended access on and a live session from another device. (1) Ctrl+Alt+Del, then Cancel; in Notepad press End twice and Ctrl+End twice: the session stays and `tornect unattended status` still says on. (2) Ctrl+Alt+End ends the session at once. (3) Open a UAC prompt (Ctrl+Shift+Enter on a program in Start), answer it, then Ctrl+End twice: nothing; Ctrl+Alt+End ends a session. (4) Win+L, sign in again, then End and Ctrl+End: nothing. (5) In a Control session the owner holds Ctrl+Alt on the host's keyboard while the viewer presses and lets go of Ctrl and Alt on theirs; the owner then presses End: the session ends. (6) With an elevated window focused during an administrator session (the helper's hook), repeat (1) and (2): the same. (7) In a Control session: Ctrl+Alt+Del on the host, then Cancel; the viewer presses Ctrl+C, then Alt+Tab, on theirs; the owner presses End twice in Notepad, then Ctrl+End twice: the session stays and `tornect unattended status` still says on; Ctrl+Alt+End then ends the session. (8) Repeat (7) with Win+L and signing in again instead of Ctrl+Alt+Del: the same |

| B17 One accept or pipe-instance error ended the host's control channel (`tornect panic`, the second launch's Show, every `tornect unattended` command) until the host restarted | VERIFIED (unit) 2026-10-24 for the Unix endpoint and the retry; the Windows loop NEEDS-DEVICE(windows) | `815aab9b`, `d08ac50f`. Unix: a failed `accept` pauses the loop (50 ms, doubling to 1 s, reset by an accepted connection) and accepts again; only `EBADF`, `EINVAL` or `ENOTSOCK` (the listening socket itself unusable) end it. Windows: the next instance is made with the same back-off while the connected instance is held, and an instance that cannot be freed, after a refusal or after a client that left before it was served (`d08ac50f`: that path used to ignore the failed `DisconnectNamedPipe` and wait on the same instance every 50 ms, serving nothing and saying nothing), is replaced the same way (`freed_or_replaced`), dropped only once its replacement is made, so the pipe's name never lapses; `FILE_FLAG_FIRST_PIPE_INSTANCE`, the DACL, the account checks and `MAX_CONNECTIONS` are unchanged. Tests (tornect-platform): `ipc::tests::{an_accept_that_fails_does_not_end_the_endpoint (EMFILE, ENFILE, ECONNABORTED, EINTR, then two requests answered; fails when every accept error ends the loop), an_unusable_listener_ends_the_endpoint, only_an_unusable_listener_ends_the_endpoint}`, `ipc::pipe_rules::{a_failure_the_endpoint_outlives_pauses_it_briefly, a_pipe_instance_that_cannot_be_made_yet_is_tried_again, a_pipe_instance_that_cannot_be_freed_is_replaced}` (the last fails when an instance that could not be freed is kept, or dropped before its replacement is made). Recipe (Windows 10 and 11): start `tornect.exe host`; in PowerShell 7 run `1..32 \| ForEach-Object -Parallel { tornect unattended status }` three times; then `tornect panic` and `tornect unattended status` both answer, and the host's output never says the control channel stopped (a "making the IPC pipe's next instance failed; trying again" warning in its log is allowed) |

Live check: a key whose signing subkey expired 2026-10-01 12:00 UTC, a signature of 2026-09-15 and one of 2026-10-15 (made after extending the subkey in another copy of the key): gpgv exited 0 with `EXPKEYSIG` for both; the judge accepted the first and refused the second ("made at 2026-10-15 00:00:00 UTC, after the signing key … expired"). A real pt-fetch was not run: archive.torproject.org is not reachable from this machine. **Limit (review, 2026-10-24; `1dd6710a`):** the bound reads the signature's own creation time, which its signer chooses, so it refuses only a signature that carries its true date: a holder of the retired subkey can backdate one. Reproduced with gpg/gpgv 2.4.4: a throwaway key whose signing subkey expired 2026-10-01 00:00 UTC (1790856000), a signature made on 2026-10-24 under `--faked-system-time 20260930T000000`: gpgv exited 0 with `EXPKEYSIG` and `VALIDSIG … 2026-09-30 1790726400`, before the expiry, the same lines an honest signature of that date gives, which the judge accepts. The SHA-256 pins still decide what ships; the release notes keep E3-4 in their build-process list with that wording, as do `SOURCES.md` step 3, BUILD-INFO.txt's signature line ("after the time the signature gives") and `CONTINUATION.md` |

## Quality presets (design `quality`, revision 2; 2026-10-24)

PR-A of the design (section 11, steps 1 and 2): the host reads, rate-limits and injects the viewer's input, and takes its
acks, keyframe requests, pings and `Close`, while a write to the viewer waits on flow control. No wire change. PR-B
(steps 3 to 8) speeds the pipeline up without a wire change; its rows follow PR-A's. PR-C (steps 9 to 17) adds
the presets, with a wire change; its rows follow PR-B's. PR-D (steps 18 to 21) adds the loopback demo and its numbers,
the Wayland `maxFramerate` request and the docs; its rows follow PR-C's, and end with QUAL-1…QUAL-7, the feature's
acceptance rows (design §9). The
design reserves decision number "M1-73", which the invitation links took first: this feature's decision row is
**M1-74** (a placeholder since `a2264ef4`, completed at the design's step 21), and its media codes 0x50–0x52 are reserved.

Logs: the two moved lines carry the session id and `ProtoError`/`io::Error` text (sizes, type codes, static names), nothing secret; no log line is new. `cargo test -p tornect-session` at `edd5ac5d` → `49 passed; 0 failed`. Findings: **L-1 (low, pre-existing)**: `InputSink::inject` is synchronous and runs inside the select arm, so while one call blocks, the session's end is not seen; the admin helper's pipe write (`tornect-input/src/helper.rs` ~439) can block while a live elevated helper stops reading. Before PR-A that was reachable from the idle loop only; now also during a stalled write, so the worst-case kill latency over all states is unchanged (one injector call). Fix for M5 (not blocking): inject from a dedicated thread through a bounded queue, or give the helper pipe a write timeout. **I-1**: during its write the picture under way is already in the ack window (the step-1 deviation), so a viewer can ack its (guessable) `seq` before receiving it and free the window early; `Pipeline::credit` keeps at most one credit outstanding (`waiting`), so the host holds at most the picture under way plus one encoded picture, and the viewer only enlarges what it receives itself, as pre-acking a received picture already allowed. **I-2**: a viewer that floods during a stall is now drained instead of being held back by the 64-frame queue and Tor flow control; each frame costs what it costs in the idle loop (an ack O(window), one budgeted inject, a counter, a ping token at 5/s burst 10), and at most one `Pong` follows each write, so there is no amplification |

Findings, all info: **I-1** a host that alternates two `Quality` values passes the viewer's "only on a change" filter with every frame: each costs it a 23-byte frame and the viewer one model write under the lock (`update_quiet`, no wake, no redraw) and nothing printed beyond one line a second; display-only, bounded by the stream's own rate. **I-2** the version line (`read_bind`, info) can be written by anyone who opens a media stream, one line per stream, as the existing "media bind refused" (info) and "something other than a bind" (debug, which the default filter keeps) lines already can; it carries only the length; with the optional daily file log, a rate limit for all three pre-bind lines would bound its growth. **I-3** `SourceRequest.max_fps` is honoured by the test card only; the portal, X11 and GDI sources capture at their own rate and the encoder paces each preset (PipeWire's `maxFramerate` is the design's later research step); either way the capture rate never depends on the viewer. **I-4** `Stats` tells a viewer of any preset the host's desktop size (rule 10 accepts it: Best quality shows it anyway); also, an unknown `[viewer] quality` name makes `config.toml` fail to load, so a config written by a later version with another preset name would stop this one starting (local and owner-written: not a security matter, worth a line in the release notes) |

Measured (release, 10 s, Best quality, `--threads 1`): 1366×768 `yuv2rgb_ms=13.8` against 1368×768 `1.1`; 3538×1918 73–103 ms against 3536×1918 `5.3`. Fix options, not taken here: the host fits every picture to a width that is a multiple of 8 (a crop of up to 7 columns, amending M1-74 (3) and the injectors' `shown_region`), or `tornect-codec` converts the first `w & !7` columns with the SIMD path and the rest itself. Speed (a standalone release build of the same loop, this container): 1366×768 1.8–2.4 ms against 11–14 ms for `openh264`'s scalar loop, 3538×1918 12–15 ms against 82–92 ms; in the demo the row on QUAL-7. Deviation: design §1 lists "a CPU YUV→RGB converter of our own" as a non-goal and §6.3 keeps native odd widths on the scalar path (decision M1-74, deviations); M1-74 (3) is unchanged |

(6) Transport — N/A. (7) Unsafe — PASS: the new GDI blocks (`crates/tornect-capture/src/gdi.rs:133` `EnumDisplayMonitors`, `:166` the callback's list, `:178` `GetMonitorInfoW` with `cbSize` of `MONITORINFOEXW`) each carry a `// SAFETY:` comment whose invariants hold (the callback runs only inside the call, on this thread, with `data` the address of a local that outlives it; the list stops at 64); `grab(rect)` reads back exactly the `w × h` DIB it made, `w` and `h` checked into `i32`; the X11 grab refuses a rectangle beyond `GetImage`'s `i16` corner or `u16` size (`image_rect`) and checks `frame_bytes` before the request. (8) Abuse — PASS: view-only stays view-only (no injector, `Input` dropped undecoded, `host.rs:1764`; choosing a screen is allowed, a viewing choice); input lands only on what the viewer saw: the `Viewport` clamps into `shown` and refuses a view outside the space (`crates/tornect-input/src/lib.rs:653`), the barrier holds moves, wheel turns and presses until `VideoAck(S)` and wheel turns and presses until a move after it (`host.rs:1695`, set at `:1152`, cleared at `:1750`), `Tracked::retarget` lets go of held buttons and keeps keys (`lib.rs:422`), a refused retarget drops the injector, sets `INPUT_LOST` and tells the observer `input: false` (`host.rs:1138`–`:1178`); the panic key, the kill and `sessions.log` are untouched, and a kill during a blocking select stops capture within `STOP_WAIT` (`tests::a_kill_while_the_source_switches_stops_capture_in_time`); the indicator's rectangle comes from the host's own capture, never from the viewer, `monitor_for` always picks one of winit's monitors or the primary, and it stops claiming control when input ends (`injected` from `CaptureNote.input`); the window's request channel is per session with room for one, so a request of an ended session reaches nothing (`ui::backend::tests::each_session_gets_its_own_screen_requests`); the V5 hold sends no move, press or wheel turn before a picture at or after S is drawn, while releases and keys go. Bounded cost: 2 answers a second (burst 4), one switch at a time and at most one a second, at most 8 answers owed, a 15 s answer deadline, frames of at most 337 bytes. (9) Fuzz — target `media` holds both messages' seeds; its 10-minute run is the NEEDS-DEVICE row above (no nightly here). (10) Dependencies — PASS: no new crate; `x11rb`'s `randr` (and `render`, both already in the app's tree through winit) and `tornect-input`'s dev `proptest` have their `docs/DEPENDENCIES.md` rows; `cargo deny check` in the gate row below. (11) §B.8.16 — N/A. **Notes (not findings):** N1 the window's V5 hold starts at the first frame drawn after the model hears of the remap, so a move made in between still goes out; the host's barrier drops it, which is the design's safety mechanism (the session viewer holds nothing, by design). N2 `tornect host` prints the same `SHARING VIEW` line when a session's input ends as it printed before, so the terminal host's lines do not say control ended (the window's indicator does); the line's format is the design's, so it is left. N3 `tornect doctor`'s `screens: unknown (<error>)` can carry an X11 error that names the display, on the local terminal only; the window's diagnostics report leaves the reason out (M1-75). The residuals re-read and confirmed as recorded: a display change that keeps the virtual desktop's bounding box or the root's size, and the administrator helper, each at most one capture interval until the next picture's news and the barrier (M1-75 (5), §B.6 *Screens*); one indicator for several captured monitors (open, §B.8.7.3) |

## Session services (design `services`, revision 2; 2026-10-25)

Clipboard text, chat and file transfer on a session's third bound stream, built in the order of the design's
§13. The design calls its decision "M1-73"; the invitation links, the quality presets and monitor switching took
M1-73 to M1-75 first, so this feature's row is **M1-76** (reserved at step 1, completed at step 30 on 2026-10-26). The
gates G1 and G2 (the GNOME Wayland portal clipboard) and the live run over Tor (step 29) need the dev VM's desktop
and real Tor; their steps add NEEDS-DEVICE rows with recipes.

| Step 12: `ServicesHost::serve` (design §6.3). The `Bind` is read at its fixed 53 bytes within the media stream's bind deadline: a silent stream is dropped, another prefix or type gets `Refused{PROTOCOL}`, a refused claim `Refused{BAD_BIND}`, and the lines such streams cause are rate-limited as the media stream's. The live wait (`live_wait` 10 s, selected with the session's end): `Stopped`, or no picture in time, is `Refused{NOT_LIVE}`; an end is `Refused{SESSION_OVER}`, after the kill switch `Refused{ENDED_BY_HOST}`. The caps: the session's policy snapshot (taken at `on_start`), its signed mode and `Live { input }` give `eligible`; the desktop's clipboard is opened only when the clipboard is eligible (through the media layer's backend, on a blocking thread, within 5 s) and the inbox made (`user_folder`, `0700`, stale partial files swept) only when uploads are; `granted` gives the caps; none is `Refused{NOT_OFFERED}`; `Welcome` has every number within the wire's bounds and the inbox's display words only with uploads. The reader gates every frame before its body (`CapState`: granted, turned off, paused; frames decoded and skipped are counted and returned in `ServicesOutcome::Served.frames`, the design's counting hook); the writer drains `close`, `ctrl` (64, never awaited: full is `Close{PROTOCOL}`), `list` (1), `clip` (2) and `data` (2), and after a `close` that lands mid-frame it writes nothing more. The stream ends with `Close{CAPTURE_STOPPED}`, `Close{SESSION_OVER}`, `Close{ENDED_BY_HOST}`, `Close{PROTOCOL}` (an unknown type, a frame the viewer never sends, a body over its type's bound or one that does not decode), `Close{NOT_OFFERED}` (a frame for a cap never granted), or on the viewer's `Close` or end of stream (nothing written back); the session goes on. | Review of steps 14–15 (security reviewer, commits `25731ec2..82eb465f`): one major finding and five minor, fixed | VERIFIED (unit) 2026-10-25 (`3ac47d79`) | **Major, a received file could land with no record**: the worker renamed a verified file without looking at a stop that came meanwhile, the stream's end dropped the workers' reports unread, a report of a file put in place for an upload already stopped was ignored, and `Complete` was queued (failing on a closing stream) before the `Done` row was told; so a file could sit in the inbox with no `Done` row, no `file_received` line and no `files_in` count, and the host could claim it cancelled. Now the worker commits to the rename by a compare-and-swap that a stop either wins (nothing lands) or loses (the stop changes nothing and the file's report always comes), the row and the counts come before `Complete`, and the stream's end handles the reports while it waits for its workers (decision M1-76 (ah), (ai)). | Step 20's `the_window_hosts_services_carry_chat_both_ways` fails under CPU load | VERIFIED (unit) 2026-10-26 (fixed at `f6dfb124`) | Found at steps 22–23, not caused by them (the row above): under load the services host sometimes ends `CAPTURE_STOPPED` instead of `SESSION_OVER` at `GuiSessions::on_end`. `MediaHost::on_end` sets the session's end before capture stops and the host's select is biased toward the end, so either capture stopped before `on_end` (the test's bound `MediaViewer` reads nothing) or the end is missed; which one is not yet known. If it is the product's order, a session ended normally can report "screen sharing stopped", which step 24's toast would then say. Recipe: build the app's tests, then as `tester` run `for i in $(seq 30); do ./tornect-tests the_window_hosts_services_carry_chat_both_ways; done` with six `sh -c 'while :; do :; done'` loops running. **Found and fixed at steps 24–25**: the test now prints the media stream's end beside a wrong services outcome (`0bb37c6a`). Under load, the failing runs (1 in 25, then 3 in 40, with six busy loops) all showed `Served{reason: 21}` beside a media stream ended `SessionOver(5)`: capture did not stop before `on_end`; the session's end stopped it, and the services loop, whose `biased` select reads the end first within one poll only, saw capture stopped in the same poll that had found no end yet (the media stream's task ran on another worker thread meanwhile). It was the product's order: a session ended normally could close its services `CAPTURE_STOPPED`. `services::host::capture_stopped` now reads the end once more when capture is seen stopped, in the loop and at the open's last check (`services::tests::capture_stopped_by_the_sessions_end_is_its_end`; decision M1-76 (ch)). ## Direct connections, Phase A (design `direct`, revision 4; 2026-10-26)

LAN-direct sessions over QUIC with both device keys pinned, Tor kept as the fallback, built in the order of the
design's §15. The design's decisions DIRECT-0 to DIRECT-9 are rows **M1-77 to M1-86** in `docs/notes/decisions.md`
(the invitation links, quality presets, monitor switching and session services took M1-73 to M1-76 first); step A1
enters them as placeholders, step C1 writes their final text. Things that need the dev VM (UDP, a real LAN, a
desktop), a Windows or a macOS machine get NEEDS-DEVICE rows with recipes.

| Step A17: what the code does where the design is silent or differs (each in the commit body of `25e9ba4e`) | VERIFIED (unit) 2026-10-27 | (1) The host's policy is read from the session (`ClientSession::transport_policy`, the code its signed `SESSION_ACCEPT` carried; `connect` refuses an unknown code), not passed by the caller. (2) `T0` is `choose_path`'s own call, made at once after the accept. (3) `PathChoice::Tor` carries `elapsed` (the `PATH` line), and `PathChoice` adds `Broken(HandshakeError)` (the Tor stream broke, or the host broke the protocol and was answered `ERROR`, bounded) beside `HostEnded`, `End` and `Interrupted`. (4) `DirectMedia` has no `services` field until step B10; `DirectMedia::bind(wait)` writes the `Bind` and applies `after_bind_close` on failure (`DirectBindFailed { error, after }`), since the stream is consumed by the bind. (5) A reason the host gave first (`OFF`, `NO_ADDRESSES`, `SOCKET`) is answered `TOR_FALLBACK{PEER_OFF}`. (6) The viewer counts the host's out-of-scope frames itself (`ViewerDirectStats::frames_out_of_scope`) and does not hand them to the link; a change of the host's scope is dropped and counted, not a fault (the host FSM enforces the viewer's scope). (7) `take_event`'s `Ok(None)` (a host `PING`, its `PONG` owed) is not a fault. *Corrected 2026-10-27 after the step A17 review (the commit body of `25e9ba4e` says otherwise and stays as written):* an envelope kind other than `BYE`, `ERROR`, `PING`, `CANDIDATES`, `CANDIDATES_DONE` or `TOR_FALLBACK` during the path phase is a fault, not a dropped frame: a kind this build knows is `E_BAD_STATE` (`ClientSession::classify`), a kind it does not know `E_UNKNOWN_KIND` (the envelope decoder); either is answered `ERROR` (bounded, `fail_bounded`) and the result is `PathChoice::Broken`. Only a future `SessionEvent` variant (the enum is `#[non_exhaustive]`) reaches the `_` arm of `host_frame` and is counted in `frames_dropped`, whose doc now says so (`34a67b32`). (8) A host protocol fault shuts the link before the bounded `ERROR`; a stop, a host `BYE`/`ERROR` or a broken stream drops it at once; every other failure closes it (raced against the stop) before the `TOR_FALLBACK`. *The close-before-fallback order had no test at `25e9ba4e`/`3f0e5a3f` (every test looked after `choose_path` had returned); it is pinned since `34a67b32` by `the_link_is_shut_before_the_fallback_is_written` and the `shut_before_fallback` check, see the review-fix rows below.* (9) The `MemNet` tests carry the signalling over a zero-latency duplex pipe, so the host's bookkeeping can lag the viewer's next frame; `a_refused_direct_bind_ends_the_session` waits for the host's link to close before the `BYE` (over Tor the `BYE` takes about half a second) |
